faq.a: Aasifah represents Arabic عاصفة (ʿāṣifah), meaning storm, tempest, or strong wind.

faq.q: What is the origin of Aasifah?
faq.a: The recorded Arabic form عاصفة is Arabic; the personal-name use of this exact Latin spelling is a separate matter.
Yes. The underlying form recorded here is عاصفة (ʿāṣifah).

faq.q: What is the root of Aasifah?
faq.a: The form is associated with the Arabic root ع ص ف (ʿ-ṣ-f), related to storming or violent wind.
Aasifah is a lexical word used as a personal name in some communities, but its meaning alone does not make it a religious title.
This record does not establish Aasifah as a Qur'anic personal name; Arabic origin alone is not proof of scriptural status.

faq.q: What does Aasifah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu it is written عاصفہ and can be glossed as طوفان، آندھی، or strong wind; exact wording depends on context.
The supplied “aa-si-fah” is an approximate romanization, not a verified IPA transcription.

faq.q: Is Aasifah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The record classifies Aasifah as feminine, consistent with the Arabic form عاصفة; frequency data is not supplied.
